paper_title: Measuring (a Sufficient) World Model in LLMs A Variance Decomposition   Framework
caption: : Meaningful Variability Share
model_annotation: The figure, titled "Meaningful Variability Share," displays a series of stacked bar charts comparing the proportion of meaningful variability attributed to two components—MVS (Meaningful Variability Share) and 1-MVS (complementary share)—across different domains and model sizes. The domains, labeled as "Health and Nutrition," "Logistics," "Personal Finance," and "Travel and Transportation," are presented as separate subplots arranged horizontally. Within each subplot, two models are compared: "70B llama" and "8B llama," with the model name appearing on the x-axis. The y-axis, common to all subplots, represents the proportion of variability, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0. Each bar is composed of two segments: a lower green segment representing MVS and an upper blue segment representing 1-MVS. The legend at the bottom confirms the color coding. Across all domains, the MVS share (green) for the 70B llama model is consistently higher than that for the 8B llama model. For instance, in "Health and Nutrition," the MVS share for 70B llama is approximately 0.58, while for 8B llama it is about 0.39. The 1-MVS share (blue) follows the inverse pattern, being lower for the larger model. The "Personal Finance" domain shows the most significant difference, with the 70B llama model having an MVS share of about 0.72, compared to the 8B llama's share of approximately 0.36. The chart visually emphasizes that larger models (70B) capture a greater proportion of meaningful variability in these domains compared to smaller models (8B).
